newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba to market DVD player in November.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba to market DVD player in November.

text.p: Japan's Toshiba Corp. said Thursday it would start selling its eagerly awaited digital video disc (DVD) player in Japan this November, aiming to become one of the first companies to come out with the next-generation recording system.
DVD has large storage capacity and is expected to eventually make videocassette recorders, compact disc players and CD-ROMs obsolete.
The electronics giant said it would start selling the DVD player for 77,000 yen ($700) as of Nov. 1, the same day as rival Matsushita Electric Industrial Co. Ltd.
"Toshiba's new product launch is the company's first step to building a wide line-up of products and systems (for DVDs)," Toshiba said.
If all goes well, the company may start selling the electronic gadget in the United States by as early as the end of this year, it added.
The DVD system uses new laser technology to store up to 4.7 gigabytes of data on each side of a disc, enough to record 133 minutes of film and sound.

Toshiba said worldwide demand for DVD-related hardware is expected to reach 120 million units in the year 2000. Together with software and applications, the DVD market has the potential to be worth billions of dollars.
Toshiba is one of 10 companies, mostly Japanese, which developed the DVD system.
Matsushita said late August it would launch two DVD models in Japan on Nov. 1 at prices of 79,800 yen ($725) and 98,000 yen ($890).

Toshiba said Time Warner Inc. is considering launching DVD software in the United States this year, and added that if the U.S. company does that, Toshiba will introduce its DVD player in the United States this year too.
